questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a city which would feel like home. I had applied for a few different destinations in Europe and I'm happy I ended up in Amsterdam.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was more difficult being away from home than I had anticipated.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - VU is very structured and much easier and faster to get in contact with than KU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a whole canvas page with all the information you needed. You could also go to the international office or write them an email. They usually respond within one day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are different options. You can either live in a shared facility, there's two different ones: the red tower where you share both a kitchen and bathroom with your floormates or the green tower where you share a kitchen but have your own bathroom. You can also stay in an apartment where you share with less people but I don't really know anything about that.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a kitchen where you can cook, but there is no oven. It is an okay kitchen to live with for a semester but not in the greatest condition.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I recommend staying in the green tower because you get all the perks of the social life and meeting people who become your close friends while still being able to have privacy and stay in your room if you want to do that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you have the option, then find accommodation in Uilenstede! That's where I met all my friends and it's really nice to live so close to the uni and also with all your friends. Also the rooms look better than the photos on the website in my opinion and the whole area of Uilenstede is very lovely to walk around in, there are cafes and bars and a lot of life because everyone living there is a student.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A little bit stressful because there were a few steps between which I had to wait for them to approve before I could move forward. It was stressful because I needed to be officially registered at the uni before I could apply for housing. But the process is very straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive emails about all the steps you have to go through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or email the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the uni has periods instead of semesters. This makes finding courses that don't overlap a bit more tricky, but as long as you keep it in mind, it will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some courses I took were first year level making them really easy because it was a lot of repetition from stuff I already learned at home, which was nice because there wasn't as much pressure. 
Other courses were very interesting because they were completely new to me, but then that of cause I had to spend more time studying for them. 
In general I would say that the level is not higher than at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Nearly only lectures for all my classes, whereas we have more seminars as KU. The style is more interactive which is something you have to get used to. The seminars I did have were way less structured and not very helpful compared to KU. Also be aware that in some courses, attendance is mandatory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
P1: Comparative Politics: Democracies and Other Regimes (DAK) + Philosophy and the Ethics of Political Violence: Peace, War and Terrorism (valgfag)
P2: EU Governance in an International Context (EP) + The Governance and Politics of Social Problems (DAK+EP)
P3: Philosophy CIS L&S-MKDA (valgfag)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them. Obviously you have to take the courses which substitute DAK and EP, but two of them were also really easy so that was great. I also liked both of my electives - the one in P1 because it is kind of like PT but with a twist and focus on conflicts and the one in P3 because it was focused on African philosophy which I thought was an interesting point of view.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general it is a little less expensive than in Denmark to get coffee or go out to eat at restaurants. Supermarkets are generally the same level of cost as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a sportscenter at campus Uilenstede which has a lot of fun classes - I really recommend the zumba class, the pump class and the step class.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to classes at the sportscenter because you get to meet new people and it is also a fun way to hang out with your friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Utrecht is a lovely city if you're looking for a trip out of Amsterdam. I spent most of my time in Amsterdam getting familiar with the city and going to cafes and restaurants with my friends, it is such a great city to wander around in! I recommend the areas De Pijp and Jordaan. Also I really enjoyed going to markets - there are tons of them all around the city on different days even during the winter.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is very similar to Denmark but you have to get used to the more aggressive way of biking.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really do that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That you cannot park your bike anywhere you want - there are specific places where you are allowed and the municipality will remove your bike if it's not in a certified place.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The markets, being able to bike everywhere, the quality of food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try to get accommodation at Uilenstede, that's where you will find your friends
2. Be open and talk to people, everyone is there for the same purpose
3. Be excited that you're going to an amazing city that is easy to feel at home in

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world and getting to know everyone's cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
